title: Adds support for AWS (Amazon Web Services) PrivateLink for Atlas Stream Processing workspaces. To learn more, see Manage Workspace Private Endpoints.
Adds support for binary quantization of binData(int8) vectors for ingestion.
Adds support for setting concurrent to false in $vectorSearch queries to disable parallel query execution across segments. To learn more, see Parallel Query Execution Across Segments.
Adds support for asia-south1 in Google Cloud regions.
Adds nested schema inference to the $iceberg stage. To learn more, see $iceberg.

Adds invited federated users directly to your organization as active members when you use SAML federation and their email domain matches a verified domain in your identity provider configuration, so they no longer need to accept an invitation. To learn more, see Inviting Federated Users.

Adds user settings to the Atlas UI Data Explorer. You can now configure the time zone for date display, read-only mode, the default maxTimeMS for queries, and the display format for legacy UUID values. Your settings persist across all of your Data Explorer sessions. To learn more, see Atlas UI User Settings.
Supports faceting on only the matching children of an embeddedDocuments array. To learn more, see Facet on Matching Children of an Embedded Documents Array.
Adds support for computing min, max, sum, avg, first and last for facet buckets and grouping results across multiple fields with nested facets.
Shows the outbound AWS (Amazon Web Services) account IDs that you use to set up private networking in the Atlas UI.
Fixes a bug where Streams Monitoring showed 0 for processor message metrics when no metrics data was available. Streams Monitoring now shows that no data is available instead of 0.
Adds support for a cron schedule in the $source stage. To learn more, see Cron Schedule.
Adds support for us-west1 in Google Cloud and northeurope, eastasia, and southeastasia in Azure (Microsoft Azure) regions.

Improves change stream source initial sync so that it can copy collections whose _id values span multiple BSON types, such as ObjectId, string, numeric, date, and UUID. To learn more, see Configure Multi-Collection Initial Sync.
Adds support for vertical autoscaling. To learn more, see Atlas Stream Processing Vertical Autoscaling.

Updates the $iceberg aggregation stage to write files to AWS (Amazon Web Services) S3 using the s3:// scheme instead of the s3a:// scheme, which increases compatibility with external query engines. To learn more, see $iceberg.
Removes the option to enable the BI Connector for new and existing clusters ahead of its end of life. To query your data with SQL, use Atlas SQL instead.

label: General Availability
title: Adds support for Voyage AI embedding and reranking inference in the Europe Geography, so you can keep inference traffic within the EU for data residency. To learn more, see Voyage AI Geographies.

label: General Availability
title: Adds support for connecting Atlas SQL directly to a Dedicated cluster, so you can use the SQL interface without configuring Atlas Data Federation.

Allows you to sign in to Atlas from MongoDB Compass and approve delegated access, so the intelligent assistant can use your existing Atlas permissions to inspect Atlas metadata and provide targeted troubleshooting when a MongoDB Compass connection fails.

Enables you to use LDAP authorization alongside other external authentication mechanisms, including AWS (Amazon Web Services) IAM, X.509, and OIDC, so you can combine authentication mechanisms in a single deployment.

Improves the metrics experience in the Atlas UI with a uniform interface and consistent controls for metrics charts across all dedicated cluster architectures, so you can correlate metrics with events and alerts when you monitor your deployment. To learn more, see cluster metrics.
Adds support for write operations in Query Shape Insights, which previously covered only find and aggregate commands. You can now diagnose the performance of update, insert, and delete commands.

Publishes the end-of-life plan for Push-Based Log Export, which reaches end of life on February 4, 2027 and stops accepting new configurations on October 30, 2026. To migrate to external log sinks, see Export Logs to AWS (Amazon Web Services) S3 (Simple Storage Service) Buckets.

label: General Availability
title: Adds Gen2 support for M30+ Dedicated clusters on Google Cloud, allowing you to scale disk storage capacity and storage performance (IOPS (Input/Output Operations per Second) and throughput) independently for improved cost optimization. To learn more, see Gen2 Dedicated clusters.

label: General Availability
title: Adds Intelligent Workload Management, which protects cluster availability during overload by queuing operations, prioritizing critical work, and shedding excess operations as a last resort. To adjust the protections that apply to your cluster, see Configure Load Shedding.

label: Public Preview
title: Releases Atlas Infinite, an Atlas database edition that separates compute from storage into independent layers. To learn more, see MongoDB Atlas Infinite: Overview.

Adds support for streaming Activity Feed events to external tools. You can export events from the Project Activity Feed to AWS (Amazon Web Services) S3 (Simple Storage Service), Azure Blob Storage, Datadog, Google Cloud Storage, Splunk, or any OpenTelemetry-compatible destination, and events from the Organization Activity Feed to OpenTelemetry-compatible destinations.

Improves throughput for operations that require an optimized initial sync on AWS (Amazon Web Services), such as adding or replacing nodes, adding regions, and creating or rebuilding shards. To learn more, see Enable or Disable Fast Disk Pre-Warming.

Adds a Shell Syntax Mode for inserting and editing documents in the Atlas UI and MongoDB Compass, so you can use consistent MongoDB shell syntax with unquoted field names and type constructors such as ObjectId() and ISODate() instead of switching between shell and EJSON syntax.
Fixes a bug where Atlas Stream Processing did not support audit logs in us-east-2, eu-west-3, and ap-northeast-2.
Adds Private Link support for the $externalFunction aggregation stage. To learn more, see Add an AWS Lambda Private Link Connection.
Adds support for parallelism in the $externalFunction aggregation stage.
Adds new activity feed events for Atlas Stream Processing.
Adds a modal in the Atlas UI for checkpoint clearing when editing a stream processor.
Adds the Project Stream Processing Manager role. To learn more, see Project Roles.
Adds support for creating an AWS (Amazon Web Services) Confluent Enterprise cluster Private Link connection without a dnsDomain value. To learn more, see Add a Kafka Private Link Connection.
Updates the default number of cross-region network permissions for new projects from 40 to 100. Existing projects are unchanged.

Adds alerts that notify you when your cluster is impacted by connection rate limits, so you can identify when your clients are offering more new connections than your cluster can process and act before connections are dropped.

label: General Availability
title: Adds a FOCUS Cost and Usage Report that presents your billing cost and usage data in the industry-standard FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification (FOCUS) 1.3 format, so you can reconcile and integrate your billing data with FinOps and cross-vendor cost-management tools.

Allows you to manage indexes in Data Explorer when you have the Project Index Manager role combined with the Project Data Access Read Only or Project Data Access Read/Write role, so you can grant granular access to index controls without granting access to data.
Adds doubleMetaphone token filter.
Adds support for the $vectorSearch pipeline stage.
Improves how Kafka source stream processors distribute processing across partitions during periods of heavy load, resulting in more even processing.
Adds stream processor CPU and memory usage to the Monitoring tab in the Atlas UI. To learn more, see Monitor Stream Processor Workspaces in the Atlas UI.
Supports sorted index to pre-sort documents in ascending or descending order at index-time instead of sorting at query-time.
Adds englishMinimalStemming token filter.
Reverts the Atlas UI read preference back to reading from the primary unless the primary is unavailable. This restores the behavior that was in place before March 2026.

Adds support for setting an operations contact for your Atlas organization, similar to existing security and billing contacts. This contact, which does not need to be an Atlas user, receives operational notifications from MongoDB.

Adds support for downloading cloud backup snapshots through a private endpoint for Google Cloud, matching existing AWS (Amazon Web Services) and Azure (Microsoft Azure) support. This enhances security by keeping backup download traffic off the public internet.
Improves performance of the Projects page by adding pagination, helping you load and navigate large lists of projects more quickly.

Improves Atlas resiliency during cloud provider regional outages. When you start a scaling or region-change operation that requires tearing down resources in an unhealthy region, Atlas now bypasses that teardown safely instead of stalling, so your operation completes without manual intervention. To learn more, see Reconfigure a Replica Set During a Regional Outage.

Extends data validation coverage to clusters that use CMK (customer-managed key). Atlas runs data validation automatically as a background job to detect silent data corruption, so this requires no action from you.

Adds automatic scaling of the maximum oplog size on dedicated clusters that use EBS (non-NVMe) storage. When you change the storage size, Atlas now resizes the oplog to match the new disk size, even if you never set a custom oplog size. To learn more, see Oplog Size Behavior.

label: General Availability
title: Adds support for additional payment methods in Atlas billing, including Link, ACH, SEPA Direct Debit, Google Pay, and Revolut, in addition to existing credit card and PayPal options.

label: General Availability
title: Adds support for Collection- and Database-Level Restore, allowing you to restore an individual database or collection directly into a live cluster through the Atlas UI or the Atlas Administration API. This gives you fine-grained control over recovery workflows, so you can fix isolated data issues without affecting the rest of your application.
Adds general availability support for writing to Apache Iceberg tables using the $iceberg aggregation stage. To learn more, see $iceberg.
Makes support for nested embedding in MongoDB Vector Search indexes generally available.
Adds Native Reranking through the $rerank aggregation stage for reordering input documents by using Voyage AI's reranking models.
Increases the maximum number of buckets to 10000 for number and date facets.
Adds support for regional failover. To learn more, see Failover Processors.
Improves error messaging when creating a pipeline in the Atlas UI.
Overhauls the UI experience for creating and editing a stream processor. To learn more, see Create a Stream Processor.

Adds read-only access to the Edit Connection page for in-use connections from a connection registry entry. A banner indicates that you must stop processors using the connection before making any changes. Previously, you had to stop processors using the connection to view its details. To learn more, see View Connections in the Connection Registry.

Adds an addedParallelism field to sp.processor.stats() that reports the additional parallelism the stream processor has configured, calculated as the sum of (parallelism - 1) across every stage that sets a parallelism value greater than 1. To learn more, see View Statistics of a Stream Processor.
Adds support for multi-collection initialSync. To learn more, see MongoDB Collection Change Stream.
Adds the ability to change the tier of a stream processor in mongosh. To learn more, see sp.processor.modify().
Fixes a bug where connection names could contain special characters other than ., -, , and .
Adds the ability to change the tier of a stream processing workspace in the Atlas UI.
Adds direct links to the Visual Builder and JSON editor on empty stream processing workspace cards.
Fixes a bug where the Get One Stream Processor endpoint returns an HTTP 400 rather than a 404 when the stream processor doesn't exist.

Updates the storage capacity display for Gen2 Dedicated clusters with local NVMe SSDs to use GiB instead of GB, matching the unit that other cluster tiers already use. Existing AWS Gen1 clusters continue to display storage in GB.

Adds cost-effective Extended Standard IOPS for AWS (Amazon Web Services) Gen2 Dedicated clusters. You can provision IOPS (Input/Output Operations per Second) above the baseline your disk storage already includes, without moving to a higher-cost IOPS (Input/Output Operations per Second) option.

Adds cross-region support for AWS PrivateLink when you export backup snapshots to Amazon S3, so you can distribute snapshots to S3 (Simple Storage Service) buckets in other AWS (Amazon Web Services) regions while keeping all export traffic on private endpoints and private IP (Internet Protocol)s.
Integrates an improvement to initialSync memory handling.
Increases the maximum number of buckets to 10000 for string facets.
Removes the source message consumption and sink message delivery panels in the stream processor metrics UI when the source or sink does not support per-target statistics.
Fixes an issue that returned an incorrect HTTP status code when a workspace is not found.
Fixes an invalid field in the Kinesis sink template in the Pipeline Visual Builder.
Fixes a UI issue where GCP Private Service Connect costs were not displaying correctly for Google Cloud workspaces.
Adds support for the brazilsouth and australiaeast in Azure (Microsoft Azure), eu-west-3 in AWS (Amazon Web Services), and us-east4 in Google Cloud regions.
Adds a display of the AWS PrivateLink cost for AWS Kinesis and S3 connections in the Atlas UI.
Adds support for private networking for Azure (Microsoft Azure) Blob Storage connections. To learn more, see Add an Azure Blob Storage Private Link Connection.
Adds a tier option to the Create One Stream Processor endpoint in the Atlas Administration API.

label: General Availability
title: Routes identical queries to the same search node using consistent hashing, which produces deterministic results, to improve the consistency of MongoDB Vector Search query results on search nodes.
Improves the performance of Data Explorer connection experience.

label: Public Preview
title: Extends the $similarityCosine, $similarityDotProduct, and $similarityEuclidean aggregation expressions to accept BinData vectors directly, improving performance by eliminating array conversion.

label: Public Preview
title: Enables automated text embedding in Atlas Vector Search using Voyage AI models, which eliminates the need for a separate embedding pipeline when performing semantic search on text data.
Adds support for retrieving expired and rejected organization and project invitations through the API (Application Programming Interface).

label: Public Preview
title: Adds $similarityCosine, $similarityDotProduct, and $similarityEuclidean aggregation expressions that compute exact vector similarity between two vectors within an aggregation pipeline, without requiring a vector search index.

Adds Atlas Stream Processing support in four new cloud regions: Microsoft Azure Brazil South (brazilsouth), Microsoft Azure Australia East (australiaeast), AWS (Amazon Web Services) EU West 3 (eu-west-3), and Google Cloud US East 4 (us-east4).

label: General Availability
title: Stores source fields in the Atlas Vector Search index to reduce query latency, which eliminates unnecessary document fetches during query execution.
Adds a $meta keyword searchRootDocumentId field when you use the Atlas Search returnScope operator for searching nested data.

Adds support for AWS PrivateLink cross-region connectivity. You can now configure which regions can connect to your private endpoint service. Applications in different AWS (Amazon Web Services) regions can now connect to your Atlas clusters through private endpoints.

Adds support for customer-managed key encryption on dedicated MongoDB Search nodes in Microsoft Azure, which enables you to use your own encryption keys to protect search node data at rest. To learn more, see Encryption at Rest using Customer Key Management.

label: General Availability
title: Improves Hierarchical Navigable Small Worlds index correctness in Atlas Vector Search by adding new hnswOptions index configurations (maxEdges, numEdgeCandidates) that let advanced users tune graph construction for higher recall.
Adds preview support for $vectorSearch over arrays of embeddings and arrays of embedded documents containing vectors.
Integrates fixes for latency stats for $lookup when not using parallelism.
Adds the metricThreshold object and deprecates the legacy threshold object to fix Terraform resource creation issues without breaking backward compatibility.
Introduces the storedSource option for MongoDB Vector Search indexes to store source document fields with the index and return them in $vectorSearch results using returnStoredSource.
Adds support for uploading processor definitions directly from local .json files using a new Upload file button on the JSON Editor UI page.
Adds support for Google Cloud Pub/Sub as a sink. To learn more, see Google Cloud Pub/Sub Connections.
Adds support for multi-select faceting to enable users to filter by multiple buckets within the same facet without recomputing counts for the other buckets in that facet.

Adds preview support for flat indexes in MongoDB Vector Search through the flat value for the indexingMethod option. Flat indexes provide enhanced support for multitenant workloads, delivering improved performance, recall, and resource efficiency.
Executes queries concurrently across index partitions if concurrent is set to true.
Adds support for Azure (Microsoft Azure) Blob Storage as a sink. To learn more, see Azure Blob Storage ($emit stage) and Azure Blob Storage Connections.

Enables configurable sampling for data model inference in Compass and Data Explorer. Specify the number of documents Atlas samples when inferring a collection's schema. To learn more, see Data Modeling in Atlas.

label: Public Preview
title: Adds support for vector field type on arrays of embeddings, enabling semantic search across nested subdocuments containing multiple embedding vectors.
Adds support for automated Voyage AI embeddings in the LangChainJS framework, enabling you to use MongoDB auto-embedded vector search indexes with JavaScript applications.

label: Public Preview
title: Adds support for the $rerank operator in Atlas Search, enabling semantic re-ranking of search results to improve relevance.
Adds additional metrics to the third-party DataDog integration, including database and namespace-level metrics for enhanced observability.
Adds CPU time to Query Shape Insights, allowing you to identify and optimize resource-intensive operations and prioritize queries for cluster resource optimization.
Improves independent shard scaling by removing the two-tier zone gap limitation at the cluster level and adding support for asymmetric auto-scaling range configurations.
Enables cloud backup support for clusters deployed in the Microsoft Azure government environment.

Adds the uncompressed data size alongside compressed storage size for each collection in Data Explorer. Compare these sizes to identify collections with the most potential for space reclamation after compression. To learn more, see View Collections.
Adds support for Google Cloud Pub/Sub as a sink in Atlas Stream Processing, allowing you to stream data with GCP Private Service Connect for private network connectivity.
Blocks deletion of clusters that stream processors still reference.
Allows changing Apache Kafka connection authentication between PLAIN and OIDC in the connection registry.
Adds additional validation for Apache Kafka bootstrap server hostnames.
Replaces the test icon with a labeled TEST button for Sample, Apache Kafka, and Atlas connections.
Removes the Search Query Analytics feature from Atlas. Related developer content and documentation have been retired.

Enables backup support for Dedicated clusters deployed in Microsoft Azure that have data exfiltration prevention policies enabled, allowing you to take backups while enforcing preventative controls against data exfiltration.

Introduces MongoDB Agent Skills, a package that injects MongoDB-specific engineering standards into AI agent development environments. The package provides six specialized capabilities covering schema design, query optimization, indexing, aggregation pipelines, data modeling, and Atlas configuration. To learn more, see Build AI Agents with MongoDB.

Adds support for high CPU (Central Processing Unit), low CPU (Central Processing Unit), and storage-optimized instance types for Search nodes in additional AWS (Amazon Web Services) regions, including APSOUTHEAST5, APSOUTHEAST1, EUWEST3, EUSOUTH2, AFSOUTH1, APEAST1, APSOUTH2, APSOUTHEAST3, APSOUTHEAST7, EUSOUTH1, EUCENTRAL2, ILCENTRAL1, MXCENTRAL1, MECENTRAL1, and APSOUTHEAST2.

Introduces a new alert that fires when a potentially dangerous database profiler configuration is detected on your cluster, such as profiling all operations or profiling with a zero-millisecond threshold. This alert helps prevent unintended performance degradation on production workloads.
Updates the Atlas UI read preference to default to secondaryPreferred. This change was reverted in July 2026.
Improves Intelligent Workload Management write blocking to use dynamic range-based thresholds instead of static values, reducing unnecessary write blocking during disk scaling operations.

Adds support for sending all Atlas logs, including MongoDB Search and Atlas Stream Processing logs, directly to Datadog, Splunk, Google Cloud Cloud Storage, Microsoft Azure Blob Storage, and any OpenTelemetry-compatible vendor, making it easier to analyze MongoDB logs alongside other telemetry in your existing observability platform.
Improves disk auto-scaling to trigger during long-running operations such as shard drain operations, preventing clusters from running out of disk space without requiring manual intervention.

Adds an automatic copy region option for snapshot distribution, allowing Atlas to automatically copy backups to all regions in your cluster and keep copy destinations in sync as your cluster topology changes, reducing the risk of gaps in regional backup coverage.
Improves validation for Azure Event Hub connections to ensure only valid Namespace ARM URIs are accepted.
Improves error handling for the operations to start, stop, and delete stream processors.
Fixes an issue where the modifyStreamProcessor action was unavailable for role assignment.
Fixes an issue that prematurely marked streams connections as Ready while the underlying Atlas cluster was still provisioning.

Adds support for the Download Operational Logs for One Atlas Stream Processing Workspace endpoint in the Atlas Administration API to download operational logs for Atlas Stream Processing workspaces or stream processors.

Enables project-level streams auditing by default and removes the Streams Auditing toggle from the Database & Network Access > Security > Advanced page in the Atlas UI. Audit logs are now always-on and non-deletable to meet security and compliance expectations. To learn more about Atlas Stream Processing auditing, see Atlas Stream Processing Access and Auditing.
Adds support for AWS Kinesis connections as source and sink options when you Create a Stream Processor in the Atlas UI.
Adds a real-time status (Ready, Pending, Failed, Deleting) to the Atlas UI when you view connections in the connection registry.
Improves performance of Microsoft Azure clusters larger than 512 GB.
Improves cluster scaling operations by allowing disk upscaling to proceed even when unrelated capacity constraints exist, reducing unnecessary delays during cluster updates.
Enables sending database and audit logs directly to Amazon S3 for long-term storage and compliance requirements.
Adds reCAPTCHA Breached Password Detection to help prevent use of compromised passwords during account creation and password changes.
Adds support for lexical prefilters in MongoDB Vector Search, enabling accelerated queries by reducing unnecessary computational load during query time.
Adds twoPhaseCommitCoordinator metrics to the Datadog integration, providing visibility into two-phase commit operations.
Adds port mapping support for Google Private Service Connect (PSC), enabling more flexible network configurations for clusters using GCP private endpoints.

Adds support for secretless authentication when using Microsoft Azure Key Vault with Encryption at Rest. Instead of providing static credentials, you authorize an Atlas-managed Microsoft Azure Service Principal that authenticates using short-lived OAuth 2.0 tokens. This eliminates the need to create, store, and rotate client secrets. This update also introduces support for unversioned Key Vault key URIs (/keys/<key-name>), which automatically resolve to the latest enabled key version. To learn more, see Manage Customer Keys with Azure Key Vault (Secretless).
Introduces new granular built-in roles for improved security posture, allowing finer control over user permissions.
Adds support for SSE-KMS encryption when exporting Atlas logs to Amazon S3, allowing you to use your own AWS KMS keys for log encryption.
Adds quality and usability improvements to the Data Model Visualization feature, making it easier to understand your data structures.

Standardizes Atlas Administration API rate limiting to use the Token Bucket Algorithm. Rate limits vary by endpoint set and scope (organization, project, user, or IP address). This approach provides predictable performance with burst capability and adds response headers that offer visibility into rate limit quotas, current usage, and reset times.

Adds new MongoDB Search alerts and metrics for index field limits to prevent performance degradation and mongot instability, which over-indexing can cause: - Atlas Search: Max Number of Fields Indexed is - Atlas Search: Max Number of nGram Fields Indexed is To mitigate alerts, consider switching to static mapping, applying the attribute pattern for polymorphic schemas, and auditing nGram or autocomplete usage. To learn more, see Review MongoDB Search Metrics.
Adds support for integrations with Confluent Schema Registry.
Allows writing over an HTTPS connection using $https as a final stage in a pipeline.
Adds support for Avro serializarion.
Updates index build completion notifications to clearly identify MongoDB Vector Search indexes and provide relevant documentation links for running your first vector search query.
Improves automatic recovery for clusters using Encryption at Rest. Clusters can now automatically recover after a KMS key becomes available again, even when cluster processes are disabled.
Adds visibility into alert severity levels with the ability to override default severity settings for individual alert types.
Adds the ability to view plan details, including trigger information, when reviewing cluster configurations.
Adds cloud backup support for GCP clusters with data exfiltration prevention policies enabled.
Reduces network transfer costs for MongoDB Search nodes by optimizing data replication between search node instances.
Introduces experimental solution modals in Query Profiler that suggest indexing solutions for unindexed queries.

Adds new alerting for clusters using Encryption at Rest when nodes cannot start due to KMS network access issues. This helps identify misconfigured KMS IP access lists that prevent cluster nodes from starting successfully.
Allows you to retain existing cloud backups when disabling cloud backup on a cluster.

label: General Availability
title: MongoDB Assistant for Cluster Builder helps you configure optimal cluster settings using natural language.

Adds support for changing your cluster's highest priority region to a region configured for copy snapshot distribution. Atlas automatically updates your Cloud Backup snapshot copy policy to distribute snapshot copies to the original primary region (now a secondary region).

Updates Cloud Backup to automatically take an on-demand snapshot when you change the Highest Priority provider or region in a cluster with Cloud Backup enabled. Atlas stores this snapshot in the new primary region. To learn more, see Change the Highest Priority Provider or Region.
Adds support for enforcing cluster topology (replica set, sharded cluster, or Global cluster), disk size, and number of shards with Atlas Resource Policies.

Deprecates $search.tracking and Query Analytics UI. The official end-of-life and complete removal of support will occur in February 2026. Therefore, Atlas will no longer collect query data for display in the Atlas UI for all $search.tracking requests. If you have any questions or need further assistance, reach out to our support team from the MongoDB Support Portal or contact your Account Executive.
Updates pricing for SP10 and SP30 tier stream processors from the legacy worker-based model to the per-processor pricing model. To learn more, see stream processor pricing.
Updates data transfer pricing to reflect region-specific rates for both the stream processor and destination region. To learn more, see stream processor pricing.
Adds support for AWS (Amazon Web Services) Kinesis as a source ($source stage) and as a sink ($emit stage).

Adds preview support for lexical prefilters for Vector Search with the addition of the vectorSearch operator and the vector index type. This allows you to filter documents by analyzed text capabilities such a fuzzy search, phrase matching, location filtering, wildcard pattern matching, and so on before performing vector similarity searches.
Adds support for deploying Atlas clusters on AWS (Amazon Web Services) regions ap-east-2 and ap-southeast-6, and Microsoft Azure regions chilecentral, indonesiacentral, and malaysiawest.

Adds a configurable expiration duration for regional outage simulations to solve stuck simulations. You can select a duration of 1 day, 3 days (default), or 7 days, after which the simulation automatically ends. Atlas checks for expired simulations in 24-hour intervals so it may take up to an additional day after the expiration date for the simulation to fully resolve.
Adds a Maintenance window completed event to the Project Activity Feed to confirm when maintenance operations finish.

Adds support for cross-region cloud-based initial sync between AWS (Amazon Web Services) nodes. This allows Atlas to provision new data nodes from existing nodes in a different AWS (Amazon Web Services) region by leveraging AWS (Amazon Web Services) snapshot capabilities. To further speed up data copy across regions, you can Enable Faster Cross-Region Initial Sync for AWS Clusters.
Changes connection rate limits for M10 and M20 cluster tiers from 20 to 15 connections per second.

Reduces the inactivity policy for pausing inactive Atlas Free clusters from 60 to 30 days. You'll receive an email notification 7 days before Atlas pauses your cluster. To resume a paused cluster, see Resume One Cluster. If you don't plan on using your cluster in the next few weeks, we recommend exporting the data and terminating the cluster.
Fixes an issue with token field types when faceting on high cardinality fields.
Deduplicate storage cost for string fields indexed with multi.
Supports $exists operator in the $vectorSearch pre-filter.
Adds new stream processor tiers: SP2, SP5, and SP50.
Replaces the previous instance model with Atlas Stream Processing Workspaces. To learn more, see Stream Processing Tiers.
Adds AWS PrivateLink support for the Prometheus integration.
Removes the ability to create new Serverless instances in Atlas. To learn more, see Migrate Programmatic Tools to Flex Clusters.

Supports querying, filtering, and retrieving objects within arrays as individual documents using returnScope. - Adds hasRoot operator for querying root document fields when using returnScope. - Adds hasAncestor operator for querying higher-level or equal-level fields when using returnScope. - Supports storing nested fields in array of objects using storedSource for retrieval with returnStoredSource for queries using any operator.
Adds support for OIDC with JWT Authentication for Apache Kafka connections.

Adds support for specifying the stableTfl or boolean similarity algorithms when indexing string fields as the MongoDB Search string and autocomplete types. These algorithms are applied at query time to calculate MongoDB Search scores with the text, phrase, queryString, and autocomplete operators. To learn more, see Score Details.
Adds support for configuring dynamic indexing with typeSets. To learn more, see Configure a typeSet.
Starting with MongoDB 8.0.14, the returnStoredSource and scoreDetails options must be set to true or false. Queries that specify null for these options will fail.
Supports setting the $ne operator to null in MongoDB Vector Search pre-filters.
Updates blobstore credential handling to use the new refreshDate field instead of the deprecated expirationDate field.
Skips downloads of snapshots that exceed the configured age threshold.
Improves highlight loading by always retrieving highlights from the base string field.
Adds a required memory usage metric.
Adds support to create a stream processor pipeline in the Atlas UI.
Adds support for the AWS (Amazon Web Services) S3 (Simple Storage Service) private link connection type.
Adds the Test Connection button in the Connection Registry UI to initiate a connectivity test for each connection.
Adds the tenantname, projectname, and org_name fields to Atlas Stream Processing metrics, including those exported to Datadog.
Adds lifetime cache hit/miss statistics to the stats.operatorStats of the $cachedLookup stage.

Applies connection rate limits to M10 and M20 cluster tiers to protect cluster availability. These limits restrict the number of new connections each node processes to 20 connections per second. Connections exceeding these limits are queued, and if the period of overload is sustained, some connections are dropped.

Introduces Intelligent Workload Management (IWM), a dynamic resource manager in Atlas. IWM (Intelligent Workload Management) enables real-time workload monitoring and automated safeguards to maintain high availability under load. Write-blocking, now active for eligible clusters, blocks user writes when disk space is nearly full to prevent node crashes and maintain read availability. To learn more, see Write-Blocking. If you enable auto-scaling, your cluster has the opportunity to scale up before write-blocking behavior activates.
Adds support for the Stream Processor State metric in the Atlas Datadog integration.
Adds the $function operator, allowing for Javascript execution in stream processing pipelines. To learn more, see $function (Stream Processing).
Adds the $cachedLookup operator allowing for $lookup results to be cached for a specific TTL to improve the performance of slowly changing data. To learn more, see $cachedLookup.

Adds the ability for the $emit stage to send null values to Kafka topics to support compacting Kafka Topics by using $emit.config.tombstoneWhen = boolean. To learn more, see $emit Aggregation Stage (Stream Processing).
Adds support for Cross Atlas Project for $source and $merge. To learn more, see the Replicate Change Stream Events Across Atlas Clusters section in the $merge (Stream Processing) reference.
Makes the ability to send resource tags to Prometheus an opt-in feature.

Adds a total namespaces count to the Catalog cluster metric that displays the total number of collections and indexes across all non-system databases, and adds a new default alert that warns users when Total Namespaces is over 10,000.
Adds support for $source to support Initial Sync when reading from Atlas collections. To learn more, see MongoDB Collection Change Stream.
Adds support for Stream Processing Workspaces to deploy on Google Cloud. To learn more, see Google Cloud (GCP) Stream Processing Regions.
Makes the ability to send resource tags to Datadog an opt-in feature.
The german2 stemmer is now outdated.
Changes the german stemmer's handling of umlauts, so that the German letters ä, ö, and ü, are expanded to ae, oe, and ue, respectively.
Removes support for deprecated kp and lovins stemmers for the snowballStemming token filter type.
Adds support for new token filter types keywordRepeat and removeDuplicates for custom analyzers.
Adds support for $merge to be able to delete documents in collections. To learn more, see $merge (Stream Processing).
MongoDB v8.1 supports: - Creating search indexes on Views using mongosh and Driver methods. - Running $search, $searchMeta, and $vectorSearch queries against standard Views.
Adds support for Datadog Metrics. To learn more, see Datadog Metrics.
Adds number of segments and per-segment statistics to MongoDB Vector Search explain output.
Adds the ability to facet on token types. stringFacet is still supported but is now outdated.
Introduces structured JSON mongot logs.
Exposes the Hierarchical Navigable Small Worlds graph construction parameters for a MongoDB Vector Search index definition.
Adds line items detailing support subscription charges, per project simplifying cost visualization for customers with multiple projects and reducing manual effort.
Adds support for AWS (Amazon Web Services) S3 (Simple Storage Service) connections.
Implements General UX fixes and improvements to Query Profiler, including: - Increased log retention from five to seven days. - Improved available filter selections.
Adds shareable URL support for the Query Profiler, enabling copying and pasting Query Profiler URLs for an easier workflow when working with slow logs.

Adds a new $sessionWindow Atlas Stream Processing pipeline aggregation stage that specifies a session window for aggregation of data. This allow you to run a pipeline on each "session" of activity in an input stream. To learn more, see $sessionWindow.
Supports Azure-hosted Confluent Kafka clusters via Private Link connection.

Adds a preview of a redesigned navigation experience in Atlas. The redesigned navigation provides a composable and scalable Atlas UI structure, improves the self-discovery of Atlas services, and offers clear navigation across services and resources. To learn more, see FAQ: Atlas Navigation Improvements.

In preparation for the mongomirror End of Life (EOL) on July 31, 2025, lifts the limitation that source and destination cluster versions must be the same and allows you to live migrate source clusters running MongoDB versions 4.4 and 5.0 to destination Atlas clusters running MongoDB versions 6.0 and 7.0. To learn more, see Migrate or Import Data.
Allows you to filter and view the cluster type, such as Dedicated or Flex, on the All Clusters page in the Atlas UI.

Adds the autoCompact privilege action in Atlas that allows database users with the atlasAdmin role to enable background compaction. This privilege action is supported only on dedicated clusters running MongoDB 8.0+. To learn more, see How can I reduce storage usage on a cluster?

Adds new sharding metrics, Orphan Count, which is the number of orphaned documents in the shard, and Orphan Data Size, which is the size in bytes of orphaned documents in the shard when uncompressed. To learn more, see Review Available Metrics.

Adds service accounts that allow you to manage projects in all your organizations by granting each organization programmatic access to the projects. You can use service accounts or API (Application Programming Interface) keys. To learn about service accounts versus API (Application Programming Interface) keys, see Get Started with the Atlas Administration API.

Improves information you see in your invoices, including your current invoice, and allows you to view the total costs separately from the total credit usage. You can also export invoices to PDF or CSV, pay invoices for a subscription and explore invoice cost charts. To learn more, see Billing.
Increases the vector dimension limit to 8192.
Adds a new $externalFunction Atlas Stream Processing pipeline stage that triggers processes in a specific AWS Lambda resource. To learn more, see $externalFunction.
Allow you to create additional alerts: Output Message Count, DLQ Message Count, Kafka Lag, and Change Stream Delay. To learn more, see Atlas Stream Processing Alerts.
Adds the parallelism field to $merge. The field specifies the number of threads to which to distribute write operations, which improves performance.
Supports creating $https connections in the Atlas UI.
Sends cluster resource tags to DataDog and Prometheus metrics integrations.

Removes support for SMS authentication. Only existing SMS users can continue to use this method with their current phone numbers. Atlas does not accept new SMS registrations. To learn more about recommended authentication methods, see Manage Your Multi-Factor Authentication Options.
Adds the $meta expression that returns an object containing all streaming metadata for a document.
Adds the parseJsonStrings field to the $https operator, allowing it to parse JSON Strings returned from an API call. To learn more, see $https.
Supports the createUUID expression that takes no arguments and returns UUID BSON (Binary Javascript Object Notation) type values in Stream Processors.
Adds a new configuration for Window operators to support processingTime in addition to eventTime. To learn more, see Processing Time.

Adds support in the following new regions: - Amazon Web Services (AWS) regions: - MXCENTRAL1, Querétaro, Mexico - APSOUTHEAST5, Malaysia - APSOUTHEAST7, Thailand In the second half of 2025, the IP addresses of nodes deployed to AP-SOUTHEAST-7 and MX-CENTRAL-1 might change to accommodate future growth of Atlas in these geographies. - Google Cloud Platform (GCP) regions: - NORTHAMERICASOUTH1, Querétaro, Mexico - AFRICASOUTH1, Johannesburg, South Africa - Microsoft Azure regions: - MEXICOCENTRAL, Querétaro State, Mexico - SPAINCENTRAL, Madrid, Spain - SOUTHAFRICANORTH, Johannesburg, South Africa - SOUTHAFRICAWEST, Cape Town, South Africa - NEWZEALAND_NORTH, Auckland, New Zealand
Allows you to add a Kafka Private Link Connection for AWS MSK (Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka) clusters.
Allows you to deploy Stream Processing Workspaces on AWS us-east-2. To learn more, see Atlas Stream Processing Regions.
Allows you to set protected hours for your project, during which Atlas avoids performing standard updates to the clusters. To learn more, see Configure Your Maintenance Management Settings.
Adds disk throughput and push-based log export alert conditions.

Improves cluster auto-scaling and elasticity for M10 and M20 clusters, responding to resource demands up to five times faster. Optimizes workload performance and availability, potentially lowering costs.

Introduces Atlas resource policies in public preview. Atlas resource policies define configuration standards for MongoDB clusters across your organization, with options to limit cloud providers, regions, and wildcard IPs.
Supports explain results for int8 and uint1 vector search queries.
Supports facet (MongoDB Search Operator) groupings on numbers and dates in arrays.
Adds the ability to facet on number and date. numberFacet and dateFacet are still supported but are now outdated.
Supports reading JSON documents with embedded file signatures (magic bytes).
Fixes an issue that prevented the configuration of hopping windows with hopSize greater than interval.
Supports the $currentDate expression that returns the system time of your stream processing workspace each time Atlas Stream Processing evaluates it.
Changes the executionTimeSecs stat to executionTimeMillis. To view this stat, invoke the sp.processor.stats() command.
Changes the buffering duration for $emit Aggregation Stage (Stream Processing) to Apache Kafka sinks from 1000 milliseconds to five milliseconds.
Adds the Project Database Access Admin, Project Backup Manager, and Project Observability Viewer roles that allow for more granular access within Atlas projects.
Allows you to save a cluster draft and sends you an email with a cluster link so that you can return to the cluster to continue making changes.

Adds a spill to disk during sort Atlas UI performance metric and a Spill to disk during sort is sort alert condition that reflect the total number of writes to disk caused by $sort stages. This metric is also added to the Datadog integration. To learn more, see Review Available Metrics and search for Sort.

Adds a message asking you to increase the oplog size on the source and destination clusters to prevent errors during the data verification stage of live migration. To learn more, see Oplog Requirements.
Supports configuring custom ciphers for conducting all node-to-node and client-to-client communications in your Atlas clusters.

Improves handling of Backup Compliance Policy where disabling Backup Compliance Policy becomes a two-person process that requires approvals by MongoDB Support. To learn more, see Configure a Backup Compliance Policy.
Supports VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) Peering with Confluent on AWS (Amazon Web Services).
Avoids deleting the index upon initialization errors.
Supports customizing the sort order of null and missing values. To learn more, see Syntax.
Supports explain for facet (MongoDB Search Operator) queries.

Sends the availability_zone, provider, and region replica set tags as part of the metrics payload to Prometheus. Adding these tags allows you to aggregate data by region, provider, and availability zone. To learn more, see Return the Latest Targets for Prometheus.
Supports filtering the results in the Performance Advisor by shards and hosts, namespace, time range, and date and time.
Allows you to verify your data during live migrations to Atlas.
Supports Flex clusters.
Updates the createThirdPartyIntegration API resource for the Datadog integration with sendCollectionLatencyMetrics and sendDatabaseMetrics options for sending data from your Atlas cluster to Datadog.
Supports using the Atlas Administration API to edit stream processors.
Supports Azure Private Link with EventHubs.
Supports AWS PrivateLink with Confluent.
Supports scalar quantization feature to reduce the main memory requirements of vector search by around 75%.
Supports ENN (Exact Nearest Neighbor) search using int8 and int1 subtypes.
Supports binary quantization feature to reduce the main memory requirements of vector search by around 97%.
Supports ingesting int1 vectors using the new BinData vector subtype.
Adds checkMetadataConsistency to the list of supported privilege actions for the Atlas administrators under the built-in roles.
Starting from October 31, 2024, stops support for MongoDB 5.0, which is EOL. To learn more, see What happens to Atlas clusters using a MongoDB version nearing end of life?
Increases Apache Kafka Timeout from 10 seconds to 30 seconds.
Supports filtering the results in the Query Profiler by hosts.
Fixes the partitionIdleTimeout after the checkpoint restore.
Always retries processors when the target cluster is in the REPAIRING state.
Adds more watermark and window information to verbose stats.
Ensures calls to produce messages to Apache Kafka don't hang indefinitely, even when the producer queue is full.
Supports MongoDB 8.0 and upgrades M0 and M2/M5 clusters to MongoDB 8.0. To learn more, see MongoDB 8.0 Release Notes.
Adds an option to specify a designated Atlas security contact to receive security-related notifications.
Adds the PAGESREQUESTEDFROMCACHE and the DISKQUEUE_DEPTH metrics to the list of metrics you can send from your Atlas cluster to Datadog. To learn more, see Integrate with Datadog.
Adds the ttldeleted metric to the Opcounters hardware metric. To learn more, review available metrics and search for ttldeleted.

Improves auto-scaling and elasticity for Atlas clusters to allow you to scale Atlas clusters up to 50% faster, respond to resource demands 5X faster in real-time, and optimize performance, while reducing operational costs.

For Atlas clusters deployed on AWS (Amazon Web Services) and Azure (Microsoft Azure), allows you to download the snapshot over the private endpoints in the same region as the snapshot. To learn more, see Restore from a Locally-Downloaded Snapshot.
Fixes an issue that caused Search Nodes to crash when disk was full.
Updates Apache Kafka offsets for consumer groups to near-real time.
Supports the compression.type and acks settings in the Apache Kafka $emit configuration.
Standardizes the way Atlas Stream Processing serializes Apache Kafka errors into a string.
Improves paused cluster errors.
Handles $lookup with unique connectionName inside window pipeline.
Supports collectionless $lookup syntax.
Increases the $emit and $merge dynamic expression limit to 1000.
Supports ingesting multitopic Apache Kafka sources.
Adds M10 cluster tier support for the Azure SWEDENCENTRAL and SWEDENSOUTH regions.
Fixes a bug that caused consistency issues when using searchAfter or searchBefore with search nodes.
Changes the behavior of indexes with failed synonyms mapping so that queries which don't use the affected synonyms mapping can run successfully.
Supports ingesting float32 and int8 vectors using the new BSON vector type.
Adds support for the matchCriteria field to the text operator.
Supports synonyms in phrase queries.
Supports using the mongosh command or driver helper methods to create, retrieve, edit, or delete MongoDB Search indexes on M0, M2, or M5 Atlas clusters.
Transitions indexes where the index objects limit is reached to a queryable STALE state.
Supports indexing token types in embedded documents.
Sends an email if your live migration process is successful, pending 12 hours after the cutover, or has failed.
Adds the Cache Ratio metric. A high cache fill ratio indicates that most data requests are being served from memory, leading to faster query performance and reduced disk I/O.
Adds a Private Preview program for Online Archive for Atlas clusters deployed on Google Cloud.
Supports using a customer-managed key (CMK) from Azure Key Vault (AKV) to further encrypt your data at rest in Atlas. To learn more, see Manage Customer Keys with Azure Key Vault.
Adds the Disk Throughput read and write metric.
Supports converting from Binary data to various data types using $convert. This allows you to transform Kafka headers into specific data types as needed.
Fixes a bug where users were unable to create stream processing workspaces in certain regions through the API.
Stream processors that use Apache Kafka as a source expose per-partition watermarks in sp.processor.stats().

Supports Azure (Microsoft Azure) Extended Standard IOPS (Input/Output Operations per Second) and Extended Storage to limited regions. For Low CPU or General clusters deployed on Azure (Microsoft Azure) in one of the regions that support extended storage, you can extend IOPS (Input/Output Operations per Second) and the data volumes' storage capacity in the Atlas UI. To learn more, see Extend Storage Capacity and IOPS on Azure.
Supports using UUID values with all operators in MongoDB Vector Search pre-filters.
Supports using ObjectId with range operators in MongoDB Vector Search pre-filters.
Supports pre-filtering using arrays with all operators.
Supports using the $not operator in MongoDB Vector Search pre-filters.
Converts auto-scaling notifications into configurable alerts. To learn more, see Configure Alerts for Auto-scaling Events.
Supports cluster snapshots on Azure (Microsoft Azure). To learn more, see Export Cloud Backup Snapshot.
Allows you to enable faster restores for AWS (Amazon Web Services).
Provides efficient cross-project restores for clusters that have AWS (Amazon Web Services) nodes created before March 27, 2024.
Allows you to export your cloud backup snapshots to an Azure Blob Storage Container.
Upgrades to Java 21. Java 21 supports SIMD, which increases the amount of parallelism the CPU can do during vector comparisons.
Supports using the sort option with boolean values.
Updates all indexes to support the sort option for number and date types.
Supports using the range operator and sort option with ObjectId types.
Automatically indexes null and UUID values if you enable dynamic mappings, which might increase the size of your index.
Introduces Search Nodes support for multi-region and multi-cloud clusters as a Preview feature.
Makes Search Nodes on Azure (Microsoft Azure) generally available for both your development and production deployments.

Introduces exact flag in $vectorSearch to perform ENN (Exact Nearest Neighbor) search for small-scale, multi-tenant, or recall benchmarking use cases. To learn more, see Run Vector Search ANN and ENN Queries.
Supports index creation on free (M0) and shared tiers (M2 and M5) by using MongoDB Drivers.
Adds resource tags defined in projects to customer invoice CSV (Comma-Separated Values) exports and invoice API (Application Programming Interface) responses.
Supports pre-filtering your data by the objectId type.

Introduces MongoDB Search Query Templates in the Search Tester, which makes querying easier with pre-written $search queries including conditional clauses like must and should, autocomplete for search-as-you-type experiences, faceting, and more. To learn more, see Define Your Query.
Introduces changes to the MongoDB Search API (Application Programming Interface) endpoints. To learn more, see API Changelog for May 31 2024 Release.
Increases shard limit for an Atlas cluster from 50 to 70.
Removes support for legacy two-factor authentication. Use multi-factor authentication instead.
Adds the ability to unlink organizations from your paying organization from the Atlas UI. To learn more, see Unlink Organizations.
Supports pre-filtering data by date fields indexed as the filter type.
Truncates large stringFacet values.
Fixes an issue where MongoDB Search didn't include the _id field for some documents in the results when using returnStoredSource.
Introduces the general availability of OIDC (OpenID Connect) Workforce Identity Federation and Workload Identity Federation.
Rebuilds indexes where the definition version is missing.
Fixes an issue where MongoDB Search triggered spurious initial syncs after certain mongod configuration changes.
Allows you to add low carbon regions and shows Low Carbon indicators on AWS (Amazon Web Services) and Google Cloud regions when you create a cluster in the Atlas UI.

When you upgrade a replica set to a multi-sharded cluster, requires that you upgrade to a single shard cluster first, by restarting your application, reconnecting to the cluster, and then adding additional shards. To learn more, see Scale your Replica Set to a Sharded Cluster.
Allows you to monitor collection-level query latency in a new Query Insights tab in the Atlas UI. Atlas supports this metric for M10+ dedicated clusters.
Adds the Migration Hub to Atlas. The Migration Hub displays available migration resources and the status of migrations in progress. To learn more, see Monitor Migrations.
Fixes an issue where MongoDB Search didn't generate results for searchAfter or searchBefore queries when scores were tied.
Adds the ability to query and sort by null and UUID values.
Updates MongoDB Vector Search queries to run concurrently by default on search nodes.
Adds disk, memory, and CPU utilization metrics to the sharded cluster metrics page UI view.
Disables a load balancer on source clusters during live migration. To learn more, see balancers in pull live migration and balancers in push live migration.
Allows you to specify yearly option in the backup policy.
Allows you to use the Atlas UI to add team members that are part of the organization or users that previously received an invitation to join the organization.
Increases the vector dimension limit to 4096.
Re-enables sort pruning.
Includes synonym queries in explain().
Fixes an issue where sharded Atlas clusters running MongoDB v7.2.0 would return an error for $searchMeta stages that contain the facet collector.
Supports archiving data using Online Archive to Azure (Microsoft Azure) storage for Atlas clusters deployed on Azure (Microsoft Azure). To learn more, see Configure Online Archive.
Supports running $searchMeta queries in the Search Tester. To learn more, see Define Your Query.

Fixes an issue where Atlas inaccurately reported the network bytes out metric that appears in the System Network chart. This release resets this metric and the previous values no longer appear. To learn more, see Review Available Metrics and System Network Out is.

Supports Atlas deployments in the following new cloud provider regions: - AWS (Amazon Web Services) - Israel (il-central-1) - Canada West (ca-west-1) - Azure (Microsoft Azure) - Poland (polandcentral) - Israel Central (israelcenttral) - Italy North (italynorth) - Google Cloud - Berlin, Germany (europe-west10)
Supports adding resource tags to projects in Atlas. To learn more, see Tags on Projects.
Introduces Atlas Stream Processing in public preview. With Atlas Stream Processing, you can process streaming data in Atlas.
Supports MongoDB 7.2.
Supports Google Cloud for Atlas oplog store. To learn more, see Continuous Cloud Backups.

Supports retrieving $search results sequentially after or before a reference point, which you can specify using a token generated by the $meta keyword searchSequenceToken. To learn more, see Paginate the Results.
Supports replica set to sharded cluster migrations on MongoDB 6.0.8+ with Atlas Live Migration (pull). To learn more, see Live Migrate (Pull) a Cluster into Atlas.
Supports cluster node disk pre-warming. To learn more, see Enable or Disable Fast Disk Pre-Warming.
Supports using equals, in, and range operators to perform exact matching and filtering on BSON (Binary Javascript Object Notation) strings indexed as the MongoDB Search token type.
Supports auto-index creation for Atlas Serverless instances.
Rejects test failover if cluster is not fully healthy.
Supports programmatic IP access list for secure Atlas communication by using customer-managed encryption keys. To learn more, see Enable Customer Key Management for Search Nodes.
Integrates push-based logging with AWS (Amazon Web Services) S3 (Simple Storage Service). To learn more, see Push Logs to AWS S3 bucket.
Supports migrations between sharded clusters with a different number of shards for MongoDB 6.0+ with Atlas Live Migration. To learn more, see Live Migrate (Pull) a Cluster into Atlas.

Adds the returnAllControlPlaneIpAddresses API endpoint that returns a list of inbound and outbound Atlas control plane IP addresses in CIDR (Classless Inter-Domain Routing) categorized by cloud provider and region. To learn more, see Allow Access From the Atlas Control Plane.
Increases the minimum threshold for archiving data after 7 days from 100 kB to 5 MiB. To learn more, see Limitations.

Makes $vectorSearch generally available for both your development and production deployments. Also makes separate Search Nodes for AWS (Amazon Web Services) generally available for both your development and production deployments. To learn more, see Node Architecture.
Introduces vectorSearch index type that indexes vector embeddings as vector type for semantic search and boolean, numeric, and string data as filter type for pre-filtering.
Improves latency when there are no mixed types in the fields you use to sort the results.

Deprecates knnVector type and knnBeta operator. Instead, you can now use the new vectorSearch index type and the $vectorSearch pipeline stage in both your development and production deployments. To learn more, see MongoDB Vector Search Overview.
Introduces low-CPU search tiers.
Makes separate Search Nodes for AWS (Amazon Web Services) generally available for both your development and production deployments. To learn more, see Node Architecture.
Makes MongoDB 7.1 generally available for all deployments.
Supports node availability zones for replica set tags. To learn more, see Query using Pre-Defined Replica Set Tags.
Provides preview of dark mode for the Atlas UI. To learn more, see the MongoDB blog.

Introduces dedicated Search Nodes for MongoDB Search as a Preview feature. This feature and the corresponding documentation might change at any time during the Preview period. To learn more, see What is MongoDB Search?.
Supports parallel queries across segments for dedicated search nodes to improve response times. To learn more, see Parallelize Query Execution Across Segments.
Adds new regions for Azure (Microsoft Azure) NVMe (non-volatile memory express) clusters.
Supports Push Live migration through PrivateLink for MongoDB 6.0+ sharded Atlas clusters.
Decomissions free monitoring.
Supports implicitly and explicitly sorting results by score.

Adds atlas deployments in the Atlas CLI so that you can work with Atlas Search and MongoDB Vector Search throughout the entire software development lifecycle from your local environment to the cloud. To learn more, see Manage Local and Cloud Deployments from the Atlas CLI.
Supports token type configuration in the Atlas UI Visual Editor.
Supports custom analyzer configuration in the Atlas UI Visual Editor.
Performs system upgrade. You might notice some indexing and querying performance changes.

Provides preview of using Terraform Provider v1.11.1 or higher to manage your workforce's access to MongoDB Atlas with OIDC (OpenID Connect). To learn more, see Authentication and Authorization with OIDC/OAuth 2.0.

Introduces the following billing improvements: - Lowers RPU billing for serverless instances with read-heavy workloads. - Supports viewing and analyzing Atlas usage with a billing cost explorer. To learn more, see Billing Cost Explorer. - Supports viewing resource tags in Atlas billing invoices through the Atlas Administration API and billing invoice CSV (Comma-Separated Values) exports. To learn more, see Resource Tags on Invoices.
Adds a new project overview that displays modules containing common Atlas actions. You can configure the project overview to display as your project's landing page.
Supports online archives as a source for Atlas Data Federation. To learn more, see Online Archives.
Supports highlighting for fields if the fields are indexed under a parent field of type document for query predicates specified inside the embeddedDocument operator.
Starts initial sync automatically in certain scenarios with sharding.
Fixes a bug that caused changes to token field mapping to be ignored.
Provides preview of MongoDB 7.0+ databases support for dedicated clusters.

Releases v2.0 of the Atlas Admin API. To learn more, see Versioned Atlas Administration API Overview. Important: This version unifies the API (Application Programming Interface) endpoints for single-cloud clusters and multi-cloud clusters under the Clusters API (Application Programming Interface) resource.
Supports cross-organization billing in Atlas for Government.

Adds the sort option, which supports sorting in ascending or descending order on fields that you define in your MongoDB Search index for sorting. Note: MongoDB Search sort option is available in sharded clusters only if you run MongoDB v6.0+.
Introduces the ability to perform text, wildcard, regular expression, fuzzy, and range searches on string fields by using the queryString operator.
Limits the knnBeta operator as a top-level operator.
Improves performance of $search with $limit.

For Atlas clusters running MongoDB 6.0.8 or later on M10 or higher clusters, introduces ability to create and manage MongoDB Search indexes from mongosh and NodeJS driver. Note: This release does not allow using the mongosh command or driver helper methods to create, retrieve, edit, or delete MongoDB Search indexes on M0, M2, or M5 Atlas clusters.
Provides preview of vector search to store, index, and query vectors using MongoDB Search.
Adds support for restoring MongoDB Search indexes from Cloud Backup snapshots of M10 or larger clusters.
Introduces fine-grained data modification and scalability improvements for time series data.
Provides preview of federated access to MongoDB 7.0+ databases on Atlas using an identity provider (IdP) that supports OpenID Connect (OIDC), including Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, and Ping Identity.
Provides Go SDK to fetch or modify data from the Atlas Administration API.
Introduces new Organization Billing Viewer role to restrict billing access to authorized users.
Supports tags for your Atlas clusters through the Atlas UI, Atlas Administration API, and Atlas CLI.
Introduces resource-level versioning in the Atlas Administration API.

Supports an optional federationSettingsId parameter in the createOneOrganization API (Application Programming Interface) endpoint to link an Atlas organization to an existing federated access configuration.
Supports tracking search terms in queries and viewing query analytics for tracked search terms in the Atlas UI for M10 or higher Atlas clusters.
Adds the in operator, which performs a search for an array of values and returns documents where the value of the field equals any value in the specified array.
Changes the operator option of the facet collector to be optional. facet queries that you specify without an operator run over all indexed documents.
Sets the limit of unique shard keys for Global Clusters per Atlas project to 40. To learn more, see Atlas Limits.
Supports one new Azure (Microsoft Azure) region: - qatarcentral (Doha, Qatar)
Supports five new Google Cloud regions: - me-west1 (Tel Aviv, Israel) - europe-west12 (Turin, Italy) - me-central1 (Doha, Qatar) - us-east5 (Columbus, OH, USA) - us-south1 (Dallas, TX, USA)

Upgrades each of your clusters that run MongoDB 4.2 to MongoDB 4.4. MongoDB 4.2 reached end of life on 30 April 2023, according to the MongoDB Support Policy. The upgrade to MongoDB 4.4 runs within your maintenance window if you configured one in your project settings.

Supports five new AWS (Amazon Web Services) regions: - ap-south-2 (Hyderabad, India) - ap-southeast-4 (Melbourne, Victoria, Australia) - eu-central-2 (Zurich, Switzerland) - eu-south-2 (Spain) - me-central-1 (UAE)

Adds the ability to pull a source sharded cluster to an Atlas sharded cluster for source and destination clusters running MongoDB 6.0.5 or later. To learn more, see Live Migrate a MongoDB 6.0.5 or Later Cluster into Atlas.
Adds scoreDetails boolean option to retrieve a detailed breakdown of the score for each document in the query results.
Updates the default MongoDB version for all new Atlas clusters to MongoDB 6.0. - Automatically upgrades all free tier (M0) and shared tier (M2 and M5) clusters to MongoDB 6.0.
Improves the IP Access List for the Atlas UI so that you can use the same IP access list to restrict API access to Atlas, and access to the Atlas UI.
Supports user-defined metrics labels from Atlas to Datadog.
Supports enabling a Backup Compliance Policy to protect your backup data.

Supports the ability to live migrate the source clusters to Atlas destination clusters for replica sets running MongoDB 6.0.5 or later. To learn more, see Live Migrate a MongoDB 6.0.5 or Later Cluster into Atlas.
Introduces the ability to edit your MongoDB Search query in the Search Tester.

Introduces generally available Atlas integrations for AWS (Amazon Web Services) CloudFormation and the AWS (Amazon Web Services) Cloud Development Kit (CDK). To learn more, see MongoDB Atlas Integrations for AWS CloudFormation and CDK are now Generally Available.
Supports simulating an outage for Atlas for regions that contain a majority of database nodes, and reconfiguring a cluster from an unhealthy to a healthy state in the event of such an outage.
Supports connecting to your database behind private endpoints with an optimized SRV connection string for sharded clusters.
Adds EU region support for the PagerDuty integration.
Adds a streamlined experience for users deploying their first Atlas database using templates for best practices.
Adds SCRAM-SHA-256 as the default authentication mechanism for database users in Atlas. To learn more, see Configure Database Users.
Supports synonyms for sharded clusters.
Supports the number data type using the equals operator.
Adds the following token filters: - englishPossessive - flattenGraph - kStemming - porterStemming - spanishPluralStemming - stempel - wordDelimiterGraph
Adds the following language analyzers: - lucene.polish - lucene.portuguese - lucene.smartcn - lucene.sorani - lucene.thai - lucene.turkish
Supports the embeddedDocuments type in the MongoDB Search visual editor configuration mode in the Atlas UI.
Adds the ability to push live migrations of replica sets using private endpoints.
Introduces Quickly Navigate with Atlas Goto.
Adds the ability to configure some Atlas project limits using the Projects Administration API resource.
Adds the ability to simulate a regional outage for Atlas.
Supports dynamically and statically indexing objectIds and arrays of objectIds and querying the indexed objectIds using the equals operator.
Supports dynamically and statically indexing numbers in arrays and querying the indexed numbers in arrays using the range operator only.
Supports dynamically and statically indexing dates in arrays and querying the indexed dates in arrays using the range operator only.
Supports dynamically and statically indexing booleans and arrays of booleans and querying the booleans using the equals operator.
Supports statically indexing arrays of strings as the autocomplete type and querying the indexed field using the autocomplete operator.
Adds a project setting that lets you configure some M40+ clusters with greater maximum storage than the standard limit.
Introduces Termination Protection for clusters.

Adds the Set Oplog Size UI configuration setting. This setting allows you to set the minimum retention window for Oplog entries. You can see the Set Oplog Size configuration setting in the UI only if you previously configured it for your cluster. For all new clusters, set the Minimum Oplog Window instead.
Adds three more Google Cloud regions: - europe-west8 (Milan, Italy) - europe-west9 (Paris, France) - europe-southwest1 (Madrid, Spain)
Improves the memory utilization calculation used to auto-scale clusters.
Adds the ability to automatically copy backup snapshots to other regions.
Improves performance for storedSource.
Adds the enableSharding privilege to custom database roles.

Introduces the Local NVMe SSD storage option in the Atlas UI for some dedicated clusters that run on Azure (Microsoft Azure). Locally attached ephemeral NVMe SSDs offer the highest level of speed and performance. To learn more, see NVMe storage.
Adds the ability to set the maximum lifetime of multi-document transactions per cluster.
Supports Azure Private Link for Serverless instances.
Enhancements to the Atlas billing experience for tax invoices.
Disallows Atlas clusters on MongoDB 5.0+ from configuring a default read concern of available.
Adds support for VPC peering for Prometheus monitoring integration.
Adds support for VPC peering for Live Migrate (Push).
Introduces analytics node tiers.

Upgrades to MongoDB Search, which include the following: - Querying improvements - Supports \w, \W, \D, \s, and \S regular expressions in the regex query. However, MongoDB Search doesn't return results for characters other than s, S, w, W, d, and D in the regex query. We recommend using backslashes according to regex standards. - Updates to email tokenizer top-level domains from the IANA Root Zone Database. - Highlighting improvements - Passage selector truncates long snippets to show a shorter snippet, which fixes the cause for queries failing when the passage is long. - Explain output for some queries might look different. If you use explain, verify that the changes don't break logic in your environment. In addition to the preceding list of changes, you might notice some indexing and querying performance changes.
Introduces moreLikeThis operator to retrieve documents similar to one or more input documents.
Introduces the General Availability of MongoDB 6.0.
Supports the facet collector on sharded clusters running MongoDB 6.0 and later.
